author: Eva Hines
title: Hunting ranch markets land for data center, sparking county review - NewsBreak
text:
By Eva Hines ,
7 hours ago
SOMERSET COUNTY, Pa. (WTAJ) -- Stonebridge Hunting Ranch is advertising part of its property as an ideal location for a large-scale data center.
According to The Tribune-Democrat, the hunting ranch, near Stoystown, is offering 400 acres for sale as a potential "hyperscale" data center site.
An online listing highlights existing three-phase power lines, access to an artesian well, and proximity to U.S. Route 30.
County officials said there is no evidence a developer is actively pursuing the site, but the possibility has sparked discussions about how data centers could impact local communities.
Planning Commission Director Chadd Sines said the county is considering an ordinance that could address issues such as setbacks, noise, power, generation, and environmental impacts.
Commissioner Irv Kimmel Jr. said the goal is not to prohibit development but to protect residents and resources.
Data centers have drawn increased attention across Pennsylvania due to growing demand from the artificial intelligence industry.
Supporters point to potential tax revenue and high-paying jobs, while critics raise concerns about energy use, water consumption, and effects on neighboring properties.
County officials expect to continue studying the issue and could present a proposed data center ordinance this fall.
They say any regulations would aim to balance economic development with community protections.
